title: Scaling a Sitecore Design System
description: Rebuilt a fragmented component library into a single accessible design system, cutting new-page build time in half across a dozen client sites.

image.alt: Design system component grid on a laptop screen

overview.label: Velir
overview.description: A digital agency partner building and maintaining Sitecore experiences for enterprise clients across a dozen active sites.

problem: The client's Sitecore front end had grown organically across a dozen client sites, with each team maintaining its own copy of buttons, cards, and forms. There was no shared source of truth, so accessibility fixes made on one site never made it to the others.
approach: We audited every component variant in use, consolidated them into a single accessible component library, and documented usage patterns so new pages could be assembled instead of rebuilt from scratch.
outcomes: A single component library shared across every client site
New-page build time cut in half for every team
Accessibility regressions caught before release, not after

sections.title: Discovery
sections.content: We started by cataloging every button, card, and form variant already live across the twelve sites, turning up dozens of near-duplicate components with subtly different spacing, color, and focus behavior.

sections.title: Building the system
sections.content: Each duplicate was consolidated into a single accessible primitive, documented with usage guidance, and rolled out to one site at a time so editors never lost access to a working page mid-migration.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: Within two quarters every client site was pulling from the same library. New landing pages that used to take a sprint to build now ship in a day, and accessibility audits come back clean by default.

title: Modernizing a Legacy LAMP Storefront
description: Migrated a decade-old PHP storefront to a component-driven React front end, improving Lighthouse performance scores from 42 to 96.

image.alt: Before and after storefront performance dashboard

overview.label: HMC Ad
overview.description: A marketing agency running e-commerce storefronts for mid-size retail clients on a decade-old PHP stack.

problem: A decade of incremental PHP changes had left the storefront slow and risky to touch. Every deploy carried a real chance of breaking checkout, and Lighthouse scores had drifted down into the low 40s.
approach: We migrated the front end page by page to a component-driven React architecture, replacing server-rendered templates with typed, testable components and trimming a decade of unused CSS along the way.
outcomes: Lighthouse performance scores climbed from 42 to 96
Checkout deploys went from high-risk to routine
New landing pages ship in days instead of weeks

sections.title: Discovery
sections.content: A full audit of the PHP templates turned up years of dead CSS, inline styles, and duplicated markup — the biggest single drag on both performance and developer confidence.

sections.title: The migration
sections.content: Pages were rebuilt one at a time behind a feature flag, letting the team validate each migrated page against the live storefront before cutting traffic over.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: Lighthouse scores rose from 42 to 96 and stayed there, and the team now ships new landing pages in days instead of the weeks it used to take to touch the old templates safely.

title: Accessible Booking Flow Redesign
description: Redesigned a multi-step booking flow to meet WCAG 2.1 AA, reducing support tickets tied to form errors by 60%.

image.alt: Accessible multi-step form on a tablet

overview.label: Freelance
overview.description: A small business client offering appointment-based services through a multi-step online booking flow.

problem: The existing booking flow failed keyboard navigation and screen reader testing at nearly every step, and support tickets tied to confusing form errors were piling up week over week.
approach: We redesigned the flow around clear focus order, inline validation, and accessible error messaging, then retested against WCAG 2.1 AA end to end before launch.
outcomes: Support tickets tied to form errors dropped by 60%
Full keyboard and screen reader support across every step
WCAG 2.1 AA conformance verified end to end

sections.title: Discovery
sections.content: A screen reader walkthrough of the existing flow surfaced missing labels, an unpredictable focus order, and error messages that were never announced to assistive technology.

sections.title: The redesign
sections.content: Each step was rebuilt around a predictable focus order, associated labels, and inline validation that announces errors as soon as they occur instead of only on submit.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: Support tickets tied to form errors dropped by 60% in the first month, and the flow now passes WCAG 2.1 AA testing with both keyboard-only and screen reader users.

title: Charity Microsite Launch
description: Shipped a fast, donation-ready microsite for a nonprofit client in three weeks, from wireframes to a fully themed CMS-driven build.

image.alt: Nonprofit donation page on a mobile device

overview.label: HMC Ad
overview.description: A nonprofit client needing a donation-ready microsite in place before an approaching fundraising deadline.

problem: With a fundraising deadline three weeks out, the nonprofit needed a fully themed, donation-ready microsite fast, and had no in-house engineering support to maintain it afterward.
approach: We moved straight from wireframes into a CMS-driven build, keeping the component count small and the donation flow simple so content editors could launch and iterate without engineering help.
outcomes: Fully themed microsite shipped in three weeks
First donations processed within hours of going live
Content editors manage the site with no engineering support

sections.title: Discovery
sections.content: With three weeks to launch, the priority was identifying the smallest set of page templates and components that could support the full donation campaign.

sections.title: The build
sections.content: Wireframes moved straight into a CMS-driven build on a small, reusable component set, so the client's team could assemble new campaign pages without engineering support.

sections.title: Results
sections.content: The site launched on schedule and processed its first donations within hours. The nonprofit's own team has since launched two more campaign pages without any developer involvement.
